# #9167: the SHARED policy-verdict corpus.
#
# One file, read by BOTH the Go simulator's test (pkg/policymatch) and the Rust
# enforcer's test (userspace-dp/src/policy_verdict_corpus_9167.rs). It is the
# policy-tier equivalent of testdata/nat_match_prefix_corpus.txt (#7481).
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS. `show security match-policies` had no independent oracle.
# Where pkg/policymatch does not share code with the Go write path it mirrors
# userspace-dp/src/policy.rs's tier walk BY HAND, and a hand mirror drifts:
# #6505 taught the Rust junos-host gate the #4569 fragment-associated deny and
# touched userspace-dp/src/policy.rs, policy_snapshot_error.rs, policy_tests.rs,
# _Log.md and docs/feature-gaps.md -- NO Go at all. The Go simulator kept
# reporting PERMIT / "local delivery" for a host-bound fragment the box DROPS,
# and it was fixed 71 commits later by writing ANOTHER hand mirror (#6576),
# which re-creates the same dependency on someone remembering two places.
#
# THE ORACLE IS THIS FILE'S EXPECTATION COLUMN, and that is the whole point: it
# is authored from the Junos semantics and produced by NEITHER implementation.
# Go compiles the config and runs pkg/policymatch.Match; Rust parses the
# snapshot and runs evaluate_policy_result_with_icmp; each compares to the
# column. Neither calls the other, so neither can agree with the other by
# construction -- the vacuity the issue names.
#
# WHAT IS COMPARED, and it is deliberately the operator-visible triple:
#   action     permit | deny | reject   -- the verdict the show surface prints
#   policy     the matched policy NAME, or `-` for the default-policy verdict
# The Rust side additionally checks the runtime POLICY ID agrees with the id the
# Go side stamps, which is what makes `RuntimePolicyIDs` a CHECKED shared helper
# rather than an unchecked one.
#
# FORMAT
#   case <name>              start a case
#   set ...                  a config line (flat-set syntax, applied in order)
#   q <from> <to> <src> <dst> <proto> <sport> <dport> <action> <policy>
#   ... [frag]               an optional 10th token marking a NON-FIRST FRAGMENT:
#                            Go sets Query.NonFirstFragment, Rust evaluates with
#                            l4_present = false. Its ports are ignored.
#   A query whose <to> is `junos-host` is HOST-BOUND: Go routes it through
#   matchJunosHost, Rust through evaluate_junos_host_policy_l3_aware (whose `None`
#   is local delivery, written here as `permit -`).
#   end                      end of case
# Blank lines and #-comments are ignored. `-` in the policy column means the
# default-policy verdict (no rule matched).
#
# ADDING A ROW: add it here and BOTH languages assert it. A row only one side
# knows about cannot exist, which is the property two hand-maintained lists do
# not have.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tier 1
case exact-zone-pair-permit
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow then permit
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit p-allow
q untrust trust 10.0.2.5 10.0.1.5 tcp 1234 80 deny -
end

# The default-policy verdict on BOTH postures. Without the permit-all row a
# corpus can pass while the default action is hard-wired to deny.
case default-policy-permit-all
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit -
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tier ordering
# First-match-wins WITHIN a zone pair: the deny is authored first and must win
# over the later permit for the port it names, while the permit still takes
# every other port. A reader that sorted or last-won would pass the first row
# and fail the second.
case first-match-wins-within-a-pair
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set applications application app-ssh protocol tcp
set applications application app-ssh destination-port 22
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-ssh match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-ssh match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-ssh match application app-ssh
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-deny-ssh then deny
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-allow then permit
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 22 deny p-deny-ssh
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit p-allow
end

# An exact zone-pair (tier 1) OUTRANKS a scoped global (tier 4) that also
# matches the same tuple.
case exact-pair-outranks-scoped-global
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy zp-allow match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy zp-allow match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy zp-allow match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy zp-allow then permit
set security policies global policy g-deny match from-zone trust
set security policies global policy g-deny match to-zone untrust
set security policies global policy g-deny match source-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny match destination-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny match application any
set security policies global policy g-deny then deny
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit zp-allow
end

# A scoped global applies where its scope matches and NOT elsewhere. The second
# row is the one that fails if a scope set is read as the all-zones wildcard.
case scoped-global-applies-only-in-scope
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/2 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.3.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security zones security-zone dmz interfaces ge-0/0/2.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set security policies global policy g-deny match from-zone trust
set security policies global policy g-deny match source-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny match destination-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny match application any
set security policies global policy g-deny then deny
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny g-deny
q dmz untrust 10.0.3.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit -
end

# An UNSCOPED global applies to every zone pair.
case unscoped-global-applies-everywhere
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/2 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.3.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security zones security-zone dmz interfaces ge-0/0/2.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set security policies global policy g-deny-all match source-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny-all match destination-address any
set security policies global policy g-deny-all match application any
set security policies global policy g-deny-all then deny
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny g-deny-all
q dmz untrust 10.0.3.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny g-deny-all
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- wildcards
# `from-zone any` / `to-zone any` zone-pair rules (tier 2/3) and their
# precedence over the global tier.
case zone-pair-wildcards
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/2 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.3.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security zones security-zone dmz interfaces ge-0/0/2.0
set security policies default-policy permit-all
set security policies from-zone any to-zone untrust policy any-to-untrust-deny match source-address any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone untrust policy any-to-untrust-deny match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone untrust policy any-to-untrust-deny match application any
set security policies from-zone any to-zone untrust policy any-to-untrust-deny then deny
q trust untrust 10.0.1.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny any-to-untrust-deny
q dmz untrust 10.0.3.5 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny any-to-untrust-deny
q trust dmz 10.0.1.5 10.0.3.5 tcp 1234 80 permit -
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- addresses
# A source-scoped rule: the address book is part of the snapshot, and a reader
# that ignored the address match would permit both rows.
case source-address-scoping
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security address-book global address a-lab 10.0.1.100/32
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-lab match source-address a-lab
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-lab match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-lab match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy p-lab then permit
q trust untrust 10.0.1.100 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 permit p-lab
q trust untrust 10.0.1.101 10.0.2.5 tcp 1234 80 deny -
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the #6576 escape
# THE demonstrated escape this corpus exists for. #6505 taught the RUST junos-host
# gate the #4569 fragment-associated deny and touched no Go, so the Go simulator
# reported PERMIT for a host-bound NON-FIRST FRAGMENT the box DROPS. A non-first
# fragment carries no L4 header, so the port-bearing `junos-ssh` DENY cannot match
# it and the walk falls through to the later permit -- UNLESS the skipped deny's
# L3 OVERLAPS the fragment, in which case the permit is failed closed and the drop
# is attributed to that deny. The last row is the control: a fragment whose source
# does NOT overlap the deny is still delivered.
case junos-host-fragment-associated-deny
set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.1.1/24
set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.2.1/24
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0.0
set security zones security-zone untrust interfaces ge-0/0/1.0
set security policies default-policy deny-all
set security address-book global address trust-net 10.0.0.0/8
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy block-host-ssh match source-address trust-net
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy block-host-ssh match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy block-host-ssh match application junos-ssh
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy block-host-ssh then deny
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy permit-host-all match source-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy permit-host-all match destination-address any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy permit-host-all match application any
set security policies from-zone trust to-zone junos-host policy permit-host-all then permit
q trust junos-host 10.0.1.5 10.0.1.1 tcp 1234 22 deny block-host-ssh
q trust junos-host 10.0.1.5 10.0.1.1 tcp 1234 80 permit permit-host-all
q trust junos-host 10.0.1.5 10.0.1.1 tcp 0 0 deny block-host-ssh frag
q trust junos-host 192.168.9.9 10.0.1.1 tcp 0 0 permit permit-host-all frag
end
